summary: One consolidation block, no new research route. Retracted three of my own claims and fixed the isolation convention: with B open, the isolation radius of a lattice aZ^2 is a, not a/2 (3/5 was the packing radius). Corrected consequences: (6/5)Z^2 therefore satisfies ISO(r) for r in (1,6/5] and refutes only the r>sqrt2 hypothesis actually printed in WEAKEST.md; the separate claim that local finiteness plus 1-density gives SOME gap >1 is refuted by Z^2 instead (r*=1, covering radius 0.7071). Retracted the (W)/(W2) 'same hypothesis' reading: (W2) implies (W), not conversely, with a closed 0.75-dense counterexample, so (W) is the minimal input and (W2) is unneeded extra strength. Consolidated the far-field decoupling note, the ledger and the repaired self-avoidance lemma into the corrected cyclic-locus map, flagging the two different 'Lemma D's. Independent scrutiny: far-field decoupling gives no no-go for proper colourings, since its perturbation class breaks properness and any palette-only no-go would decide chi>6; the surviving asymmetry is near-field-to-far-field, not the reverse.
verified_results: GRADE [A] Isolation convention (corrected): for L = aZ^2 with B open, max{r : L cap B(x,r) = {x}} = a. a=1: r*=1, covering radius 0.7071 <= 1, so (LF) + 1-density does NOT imply ISO(r) for any r > 1. a=6/5: r*=1.2, covering radius 0.8486, so it satisfies ISO(r) for r in (1,1.2] and does not refute ISO with gap > 1 — it refutes only r > 6/5, which covers WEAKEST.md's printed r > sqrt2 = 1.4142. Both statements are about closed, locally finite, 1-dense sets and say nothing about colourings.

GRADE [A] (W) does not imply (W2). L = {0} union the circles S(0,3k/2), k >= 1, is closed, 0.75-dense, has |L cap B(0,1.2)| = 1 (so (W) with R = 1.2) and |L cap B(y,2)| infinite for every y (every radius-2 ball cuts one of the 1.5-spaced circles in an arc). Hence (W2) is strictly stronger, not equivalent; only (W) is needed by the transfer.

GRADE [P]+[C] Consolidated minimal dependency proposition: (W_R) with R > 1 implies Prop. 7.1 at k=6, via the disk B(y,rho) with rho in (1,R) chosen off the finitely many radii |p-y| (so boundary-avoidance is derived, not assumed), inradius rho > 1 >= mesh, L_0 finite and non-empty. (LF) + L non-empty implies (W_R) for every R. (Iso_r) with r > 1 implies (W_R) for every R < r. Nothing in the record implies (W) or its negation.

GRADE [C]+[P]+[A] Proposition 1 survives the convention fix: if x in L and L cap B(x,rho) = {x} then rho <= 2, since a radius-r>1 disk avoiding x fits inside B(x,rho) once rho > 2, contradicting m12's density theorem. The usable isolation window is 1 < rho <= 2.

GRADE [S]+[P] Consolidated and checked for internal consistency: far-field decoupling (c = c' off B(x,1-eps) implies equal palettes at x a.e., sharp at eps = 0), the repaired self-avoidance lemma (recorded proof invalid; valid proof via (5.2) plus the sector Jacobian, deficit >= |D|/2pi), the ledger's R1/R2/R3/R5/R6. Flagged that the record contains two distinct lemmas both called 'Lemma D'.
conjectures: No-go reading of far-field decoupling: it does not imply any obstruction for the class of proper or weak proper 6-colourings. Insensitivity of P_x to a recolouring supported in a ball of radius < 1 is a statement about all measurable colourings; an arbitrary such recolouring breaks properness (a disk of radius > 1/2 contains unit pairs), and a palette-only inconsistency would by m10 T3 prove chi(R^2) > 6. So far-field decoupling is methodological: it forbids arguments, not colourings.

The surviving direction is near-field to far-field: self-avoidance derives i notin P_x(e) from density one of the colour class at x. 'P_x does not determine Gamma_x' is the faithful form of the decoupling claim; 'P and Gamma are independent' is too strong.

The k=6 obstruction at the accumulation site is a label-resource count, not a decoupling statement: m3's gadget of radius 1/100 has no unit pair, so internal properness is free and the whole obligation is the shell condition (gadget labels {0,2,3} avoided by annulus colours), which has four labels at k>=7 and three at k=6.
